result:
The build passes cleanly (`ns build ios` succeeds with no type errors). Section 4 (Health/HealthKit) is implemented:

- **`App_Resources/iOS/Info.plist`** — added `NSHealthShareUsageDescription` / `NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription`.
- **`App_Resources/iOS/app.entitlements`** (new) — `com.apple.developer.healthkit` capability.
- **`types/references.d.ts`** — added a reference to `@nativescript/types-ios`'s full `ios.d.ts`, since the default type bundle excludes HealthKit/Speech declarations.
- **`app/services/healthkit.ts`** (new) — direct `HKHealthStore`/`HKQuantityType`/`HKStatisticsQuery` calls (no third-party wrapper) for authorization status, requesting access, saving a 500-step sample, and querying daily step totals for the last 7 days.
- **`app/components/Health.vue`** — wired to the service: status line reflects sharing-authorization state (refreshed on every `navigatedTo`), `Log 500 Steps` enabled only when granted, 7-day list with exact label formatting (`Fri Jul 25 — 1,000 steps`, today emphasized and suffixed ` (today)`), and `Health access needed` fallback when not granted. Save failures surface as human-readable text in the status line.

One caveat worth flagging: inspecting the built binary shows `ns build ios` signs simulator builds with an empty `CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY`, which results in ad-hoc signing that doesn't embed the entitlements file (confirmed via `codesign -d --entitlements`). This is standard NativeScript CLI behavior for every simulator build (not something introduced by this change) and Simulator generally doesn't enforce HealthKit entitlement checks the way a physical device does, so this shouldn't block the acceptance run — but it's worth knowing about if HealthKit authorization behaves unexpectedly on-device later.
